program_name: Bachelor in Design and Art - Major in Design (Italian: Corso di laurea in Design e Arti, Curriculum in Design; German: Bachelor in Design und Künste, Studienzweig Design)
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English; the programme page 'At a glance' box states 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. Unlike the engineering bachelors, this programme does NOT have an all-English first semester. Based on the published 2026/27 course offering: the lecture/theory block of year 1 semester 1 is largely English (Project Warm-up DES 12 CP EN, Descriptive Geometry DES 6 CP EN, History of Design 6 CP EN, History of Contemporary Art 1 6 CP EN, Digital Design: 3D CAD Advanced 6 CP EN, Interaction and Communication Design 6 CP EN, plus 2 CP seminars in EN and Foreign Language - English: Academic Skills 3 CP EN). However the four 19-CP 'Projects' — 76 CP, roughly 42% of the 180 ECTS and the pedagogical core of the degree — run as atelier groups in mixed language combinations, and several groups are German/Italian only: Project Product Design 1.a is tagged IT/DE, Project Visual Communication 1.c is DE/IT, Project Visual Communication 2.d is DE/IT; others are IT/EN, IT/EN/DE or DE/IT/EN. Several compulsory or elective courses are single-language non-English: German-only — Design Theory 5 CP, Typography and Graphics 6 CP, Photography 6 CP, Video and Post-Production 6 CP, History of Contemporary Art 2 5 CP; Italian-only — Interior and Exhibit Design 1 6 CP, History and Criticism of Audiovisual Media 6 CP. One 3 CP compulsory course must be chosen between 'Foreign Language DES-ART 1 Italiano' (IT) and 'Foreign Language DES-ART 2 Deutsch' (DE). Approximate 2026/27 course counts by tag: ~19 courses EN, ~8 IT, ~8 DE, plus the multilingual project groups. [uncertain] — the per-language ECTS weighting is reconstructed from the 2026/27 course-offering listing (which shows only what is offered that year and assigns multiple language tags to project groups) rather than from an official language-split statement; 'Drawing 3D CAD' 8 CP carries no published language tag.
campus: Bozen-Bolzano main campus, Faculty of Design and Art, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Teaching is atelier-and-workshop based: students work in ateliers in groups of no more than 20 students supervised by 3 lecturers, and must complete compulsory safety training (Work Safety - Machinery Hazard - Chemical Risk) before attending the technical workshop courses. This is NOT the NOI Techpark campus (that is Engineering) and not Brixen-Bressanone or Bruneck-Brunico.
degree_class: L-4 (Disegno industriale / Industrial Design). 180 ECTS, 3 years. Note the national dual-enrolment rule cited in the admission document uses this class as its own example: simultaneous enrolment in 2 programmes is allowed only if they do not belong to the same class, 'e.g., L-4/L-4'.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and fully subscribed. The programme page for 2026/27 states 'Courses will definetely be starting'. Both 2026/27 ranking lists have been published and both EU quotas were filled exactly: 34 admitted in the Early Bird session (protocol 0015024/26 of 18/05/2026) and 24 admitted in the Late session (protocol 0021217/26 of 21/07/2026), with waiting lists behind each. As of the verification date all application windows for 2026/27 are CLOSED for this major — it was not opened in the Additional Application Session.
is_new_programme: No — an established programme of the Faculty of Design and Art (the faculty's online Showcase and Projects Archive covers student work 'since 2018' across the two Majors in Design, the Major in Art and the Master in Eco-Social Design). The current structure was revised for the 2025 cohort: 'From the 2025 cohort onwards, all students are required to attend the Warm-Up introductory workshop courses', and the Study Guide publishes separate study plans for the 2025-onwards and 2022-onwards cohorts. [uncertain] — unibz does not publish a first-intake year for this programme; 'not new' is inferred from the archive, the multiple cohort study plans and the absence of any 'new programme' badge, not from an explicit statement.
majors_tracks_study_plans: The degree 'Design and Art' (L-4) is split into TWO SEPARATE MAJORS with separate quotas, separate ranking lists and partly separate procedures: Major in Design (this record) and Major in Art. Quota contrast for 2026/27 — Design: 34 EU Early Bird + 24 EU Late + 2 non-EU = 58 EU + 2 non-EU; Art: 18 EU Early Bird + 10 EU Late + 2 non-EU = 28 EU + 2 non-EU. Art additionally has an Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026, interview 16/09/2026); the Major in Design does NOT. A candidate may apply for both majors but must then upload TWO different videos, one per major, and must reach at least 8/20 in the corresponding field of the practical creative work for each major applied to. Within the Major in Design there are no separate admission tracks, but from the beginning of year 2 students choose one of THREE STUDY PLANS built from the four compulsory 19-CP projects: (1) Interdisciplinary study plan — Product Design 1, Visual Communication 1, Product Design 2 and Visual Communication 2; (2) study plan focusing on Visual Communication — Product Design 1, Visual Communication 1 and Visual Communication 2 twice; (3) study plan focusing on Product Design — Product Design 1, Visual Communication 1 and Product Design 2 twice. Sequencing rules: in semesters 2 and 3 students must attend Visual Communication 1 and Product Design 1; from semester 2 onwards only one project per semester; Visual Communication 1 and Product Design 1 must be passed before attending the corresponding '2' projects. Other structural choices: 1 compulsory course from {Video and Post-Production, Photography, Interior and Exhibit Design 2, History and Criticism of Audiovisual Media} (6 CP); 1 from {Digital Design: 3D CAD Advanced, Digital Design: Interaction and Transmedia Design, Interaction and Communication Design} (6 CP); 1 from {Sociology of Social Change, Cultural Anthropology, Innovation Managing and Start-up} (8 CP); 1 from {Foreign Language DES-ART 1 Italiano, Foreign Language DES-ART 2 Deutsch} (3 CP); 12 CP Free Choice; 1 seminar (2 CP, pass/fail, compulsory attendance); at least two specialised workshop courses from semester 2 (zero credits but compulsory attendance); 9 CP Degree Project.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed. The language rule is eliminatory, not a tie-breaker: the admission document states the requirements apply 'otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure', and entry demands B2 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language. A candidate who can certify only English can satisfy at most one language and is therefore removed before ranking. Hard empirical proof from the 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list for the Major in Design: ALL 5 non-EU applicants living abroad were listed under 'Le seguenti persone non soddisfano i requisiti linguistici richiesti per l'accesso e vengono pertanto escluse dal procedimento di ammissione' — zero non-EU admissions, and the 2 reserved non-EU places went unfilled. On the EU side a further 30 Early Bird applicants and 16 Late applicants were excluded for not possessing the admission requirements. Two important qualifications: (a) the second language does not have to be German — English B2 + Italian B2, or English B2 + German B2, both work, so the programme is genuinely open to a bilingual candidate; (b) exclusion is recoverable between sessions — several applicants excluded in Early Bird (IDs 151749, 152158, 154388, 155189, 155981, 148888) appear as ADMITTED in the Late session, i.e. they certified their second language in time for the second window. A Turkish or other applicant with English only, however strong, cannot be admitted. Additional load once inside: graduation requires C1/C1/B2 across all three languages, several core courses are German-only or Italian-only, and a substantial share of the 76 CP of atelier projects runs in German/Italian groups.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a three-stage aptitude selection and a published merit ranking list. The instruments are: (1) a self-produced VIDEO (max 2 minutes) uploaded to the application portal — a prerequisite, not merely scored; (2) a PRACTICAL CREATIVE WORK carried out at home on a topic issued by e-mail about one week before the interview; (3) an ONLINE INTERVIEW of 10-15 minutes with a commission of faculty lecturers. There is NO written entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT and no conventional portfolio submission. A prior language-eligibility gate (B2 in two of the three teaching languages) removes applicants before scoring. Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad, and separately for the Major in Design and the Major in Art.
academic_requirements: Required qualification (one of): (a) a secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system; or (b) an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school-leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education AND the applicant attended at least the last two years in that foreign school system (unibz's own example: an Irish Leaving Certificate obtained after attending only one year is not enough). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain certificates — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly — and such applicants are told to contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Beyond the title, the applicant must fulfil the language requirements (B2 + B2), which are eliminatory. There is NO minimum school grade, NO subject prerequisite, NO mathematics requirement and NO portfolio-of-prior-study requirement: unlike the engineering and economics bachelors, school marks play no part in the score — the 100 points come entirely from the video, the practical creative work and the interview. No ECTS/SSD credit requirements apply (bachelor level, so the 2024 SSD recoding such as INFO-01/A is irrelevant here). National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is permitted, provided the two do not belong to the same class (explicitly 'e.g., L-4/L-4') and differ in at least 2/3 of course contents.
entry_exam_or_test: No written or standardised entrance examination of any kind. The list of instruments actually used is: (1) Video, produced independently at home, uploaded to the application portal by the application deadline — max 2 minutes, max 150 MB, formats .mov/.mp4/.mpg/.avi/.wmv, file name surname_name.format; failure to upload by the deadline causes exclusion from the admission procedure. (2) Practical creative work, carried out entirely by the candidate at home; the topic and technical indications (size of models, materials, format, etc.) are e-mailed approximately one week before the interview, and the complete documentation must be sent by the modalities communicated with the topic — sending documentation by post is never allowed. (3) Online interview, 10-15 minutes, before a commission of faculty lecturers. The only examinations connected with admission are the unibz Language Centre LANGUAGE exams, and only for candidates who choose that proof route: Early Bird — 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late — 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Only B2-level exams can be registered for. After admission there is also a non-selective third-language placement test for students who could not certify their third language.
selection_scoring: Maximum 100 points, awarded by a commission of faculty lecturers: VIDEO max 20 points (criteria: spirit of observation; judgement skill; creativity and originality); CREATIVE PRACTICAL WORK max 40 points, split into an evaluation for the DESIGN field max 20 points (spirit of observation; judgement skill; creativity and originality; design aspects in relation to implementation in the design field) and an evaluation in the field of ART max 20 points (same three criteria plus artistic aspects); INTERVIEW max 40 points (interdisciplinary interest; communication skill; creative skills). PUBLISHED THRESHOLDS: minimum 42/100 overall for admission to the Bachelor, PLUS a sub-threshold of minimum 8/20 in the Design-field evaluation of the practical creative work to be admitted to the Major in Design (and, symmetrically, 8/20 in the Art field for the Major in Art). Tie-break order on equal total points: (1) interview score, (2) creative-practical-work score, (3) video score; only if those are also equal, the youngest candidate is chosen. ACTUAL 2026/27 CUT-OFFS FOR THE MAJOR IN DESIGN (well above the published 42 minimum): Early Bird — 34 admitted, top score 99, last admitted score 57, waiting list positions 35-45 with scores 57 down to 44, 14 candidates excluded for failing the minimum score (including one with 50/100 who nevertheless missed the 8/20 Design-field sub-threshold, and two who scored 12 and 6 having not submitted the creative work at all), and 30 excluded for not possessing the admission requirements — roughly 89 EU candidates processed for 34 places. Late — 24 admitted, top score 89, last admitted score 47, waiting list positions 25-27 with 46, 43 and 42, 9 excluded on score (5 of them for not submitting the creative work) and 16 excluded for not possessing the admission requirements. So the effective competitive bar in 2026/27 was 57/100 in session 1 and 47/100 in session 2, not 42/100.
bonus_points: None. The 100-point scale is exhausted by the three selection stages (20 + 40 + 40) and no bonus mechanism exists for this programme: there is NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to the Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), NO GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), NO startup-project bonus (Entrepreneurship and Innovation), no extracurricular-activity point (used by the Bachelor in Computer Science) and no bonus for school grades, prior art/design schooling, competitions or certificates. The CV is discussed in the interview but is not separately scored.
portfolio_and_materials: No conventional portfolio is requested — unibz replaces it with a video plus a commissioned home assignment. VIDEO: created independently at home, free choice of content; for the Major in Design the brief is to show how you see the world around you, 'perhaps by confronting yourself with a two- or three-dimensional artefact', demonstrating passion for design and a way of thinking. Technical limits: length max 2 minutes; file size max 150 MB; accepted formats .mov, .mp4, .mpg, .avi, .wmv; file name must be surname_name.format. unibz explicitly reassures that professional equipment is not needed and the video 'does not have to be a perfect Hollywood production. It's much more about good ideas!'. Applicants to BOTH majors must upload TWO different videos, one per major. The upload is a prerequisite: missing the deadline means exclusion from the admission procedure (in 2026/27, several candidates were listed with scores of 6-17/100 precisely because a component was not delivered). PRACTICAL CREATIVE WORK: topic and technical indications (size of models, materials, format, etc.) are sent by e-mail about one week before the interview; it must be carried out entirely by the candidate; complete documentation must be submitted by the modalities communicated with the topic, and 'It is not allowed, in any case, to send the documentation of the work by post.' It must show spirit of observation, judgement and creativity. No motivation letter, no project proposal, no reference letters, no CV upload and no study-career Excel template are required. No page limits or character limits are published because no written dossier is requested.
interview: Yes — a compulsory online interview is the third and joint-heaviest stage (max 40 of 100 points). Conducted by a commission composed of lecturers of the faculty; duration about 10-15 minutes; the candidate receives an e-mail beforehand with the time and the platform to connect to. Content: show and explain the practical creative work to the commission; answer questions concerning the CV; answer general questions about design and/or art. Assessed on interdisciplinary interest, communication skill and creative skills. PUBLISHED 2026/27 DATES (Major in Design): Early Bird interview 15/05/2026; Late interview 17/07/2026. (For contrast, the Major in Art additionally has an Additional Application Session interview on 16/09/2026 — the Major in Design does not.) The interview score is also the first tie-break criterion on equal total points.
conditional_admission: There is no ECTS-threshold conditional-admission regime here — the ≥120/140 ECTS rule in the field schema is a MASTER-level provision and does not apply to this bachelor. The equivalent mechanisms are: (1) applicants still in their final school year apply normally and, if they gained (or will gain) their qualification abroad, upload the diploma at enrolment rather than at application — 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'; (2) holders of a foreign qualification are admitted with reserve ('ammesso/ammessa solo con riserva') pending unibz's check of the foreign title — if the title is judged suitable the reserve is lifted, otherwise the applicant is excluded, and exclusion by Rector's decree is possible even AFTER enrolment if the admission qualification turns out to be invalid; (3) the refund rule tied to this: fees paid to secure a place are not refundable unless the applicant fails the secondary-school final exam, or — for non-EU applicants living abroad — does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. [uncertain] — no separate late-enrolment window (such as the 11/12/2026 date used by some master programmes) is published for this programme; the enrolment window closes 06/08/2026 for both sessions.
ofa_rules: OFA (Additional Learning Obligations / obblighi formativi aggiuntivi) applies here in a form unique among unibz bachelors — it is NOT tied to a mathematics test. The published rule: 'The Additional Learning Obligations are assigned if any weakness is found in your basic education.' Two concrete triggers: (1) LANGUAGE — you must fulfil Additional Learning Obligations in the third language if you have not certified level B1 in the third language; (2) SELECTION SCORE — 'if you have been admitted to the BA and have achieved a score of less than 48 points in the selection procedure, you will receive Additional Learning Obligations.' The content of the OFA is defined before the start of the academic year by the Bachelor Study Council and published in the syllabi of the WUP Design and WUP Art projects (i.e. inside the Warm-Up project). The OFA is discharged by passing an exam. Practical effect in 2026/27 for the Major in Design: nobody admitted in the Early Bird session was affected by the score trigger (the lowest admitted score was 57), whereas in the Late session the candidate admitted at rank 24 with 47/100 fell below the 48-point line and therefore carries OFA, as would waiting-list entrants at 46, 43 and 42. Unlike the Computer Science ranking lists, the Design and Art lists do not mark OFA with an asterisk — the asterisks there flag the 8/20 Design-field sub-threshold failure and non-submission of the creative work.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the requirement is ELIMINATORY: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' Entry: B2 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language; no level required in the 3rd. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2, CEFR. Positions are defined by the candidate's own proficiency, not by the language: the 1st language is the one in which the candidate is strongest (B2 or C1), the 3rd the weakest, possibly absolute beginner. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd, submitted in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application. A certificate awarded by an Italian public institution is submitted as a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original. Programme-specific softening: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. In the first year of study, it is possible to sit exams relating to project-based activities before having achieved a B1 level in the third language' — i.e. the 19-CP atelier projects, which are the bulk of year 1, are exempt from the B1 gate during the first year; the Study Guide phrases the same rule as B1 being needed for theoretical courses only in year 1 and for all exams from year 2. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test (details by e-mail) and are assigned a learning path towards B2. Absolute beginners or anyone below B2 may attend a three-week intensive course in the September pre-semester session; A1 beginner courses are offered EXCLUSIVELY in that September session and no longer during the academic year, so absolute beginners must start there. During semesters there are extensive courses (4 h/week), between semesters intensive courses (6 h/day). All Language Centre courses are free of charge and target B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required. This is the 'B2/B2/none' pattern shared with the trilingual engineering bachelors, one step below the 'C1/B2/none' pattern of programmes such as Public Policy and Innovative Governance or Accounting and Finance. Position is determined by the candidate's own strength ranking and not by which language it is, so English B2 + Italian B2, English B2 + German B2 or Italian B2 + German B2 all satisfy the rule. Only B2-level exams can be registered for at the unibz Language Centre (the admission document repeats this sentence twice). B1 in the third language is not an admission condition but becomes the gate for sitting curricular exams in that language — with the year-1 exemption for project-based activities described above.
exit_levels: To graduate: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 (CEFR). This is the standard unibz trilingual exit profile and is a genuine graduation gate: a student admitted at B2/B2/none must raise two languages to C1 and reach B2 in the third within the three years. Free Language Centre courses are structured to support this, targeting B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2. For this programme the exit requirement is particularly consequential because several core courses and many atelier project groups are delivered in German or Italian only.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations held in that language. Programme-specific relaxation, unique to this faculty: 'In the first year of study, it is possible to sit exams relating to project-based activities before having achieved a B1 level in the third language' — so the 19-CP Project exams (Project Warm-up DES, Project Product Design 1, Project Visual Communication 1) can be taken in year 1 without the third-language B1, while theoretical courses in that language cannot. From year 2 onwards B1 certification is required for all exams in that language. If B1 in the third language is not certified, Additional Learning Obligations in the third language are assigned. There is NO mid-January English-B1 deadline of the kind imposed on the Bachelor in Computer Science, because the first semester here is not English-only.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways, plus a fifth route for bi-/multilingual and foreign schools. (1) The main teaching language of the final high school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1; Ladin upper secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian; for foreign qualifications, if the main teaching language is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter/document issued by the high school stating the medium of instruction must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if it is not on the degree. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be e-mailed as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, registered online in the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after filling out an application; if the application is started outside a registration period the candidate must return to the portal during one of the published periods. 2026/27 dates for this programme — Early Bird: exams 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Only B2-level exams can be registered for. (5) Secondary schools in a foreign country / bi- or multilingual schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English (B1, B2 or C1) are explicitly indicated on the graduation diploma AND all four abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, the indicated levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language; the school-leaving certificate must be uploaded under the respective language and the Language Centre decides on recognition.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants'). To be recognised a certificate must: (1) include assessment of all FOUR skills and be issued by the certification provider itself; (2) show a sufficient result in each skill as an overall grade, or have the detailed assessment stated on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the provider. If no overall result and/or level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed. There is no compensation for failed parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless the certification provider itself does so. Certificates obtained through remote 'home edition' exams are NOT recognised, except those explicitly flagged in the list. Certificates covering single skills issued by different organisations are not accepted. Certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational institutions, and placement-test results are not recognised. Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff are not recognised, and DAAD certificates are expressly NOT recognised. Validity: international language certificates must have been obtained within the five years preceding submission, counting whole calendar years from 1 January. Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: TWO sessions only for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — this major has no third session (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO given below). Early Bird Application: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, with the video upload due by the same deadline, 28/04/2026 noon. Late Application (EU citizens only): 28/05/2026 - 02/07/2026 by noon local time = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-02, video upload by 02/07/2026 noon. NOTE the Late window closes SIX DAYS EARLIER than the engineering/economics bachelors' 08/07/2026 — it is programme-specific. There is NO Additional Application Session for the Major in Design in 2026/27: the programme's own admission document lists only two sessions, and the university's Additional Application Session page lists only the Bachelor in Design and Art - Major in Art and the Master in Critical Creative Practices for the Faculty of Design and Art. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in the first session may apply again in the second (in 2026/27 at least six candidates excluded in Early Bird were admitted in the Late session).
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the Early Bird Application, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, with the video uploaded to the application portal by 28/04/2026 noon, the online interview on 15/05/2026 and the ranking list by 27/05/2026. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application, pay a non-refundable €50 application fee, are ranked on a separate list against a separate 2-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. In 2026/27 all 5 non-EU applicants to the Major in Design were excluded at the language gate, so both non-EU places went unused.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants — the critical third category for Turkish and other non-EU nationals: (1) citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; (2) non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39 paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 — for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. These applicants apply directly to the University and must submit a copy of the valid permit to stay; if the permit has expired a renewal request must be attached. A permit to stay for STUDY reasons or a visa for tourism is NOT sufficient. Critical warning reproduced verbatim in the admission document: if the permit is not uploaded in the application portal, the applicant 'will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin' — which for this programme means losing access to the Late session and to 56 of the 58 EU places, and competing instead for just 2 places.
places_quotas: Two separate quotas for the Major in Design in 2026/27, across two sessions. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application 34 places, Late Application 24 places (58 EU in total — the programme page and brochure summarise this as 'Places available: 58 EU + 2 non-EU'). Non-EU citizens living abroad: Early Bird Application 2 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. Carry-over rule: for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only, any places remaining unfilled after the Early Bird session are offered in the Late Application. Actual 2026/27 uptake: BOTH EU quotas were filled exactly — 34 admitted in Early Bird with an 11-person waiting list, 24 admitted in the Late session with a 3-person waiting list — while ZERO of the 2 non-EU places were filled because all 5 non-EU applicants were excluded at the language gate. Contrast with the sibling Major in Art: 18 EU Early Bird + 10 EU Late + 2 non-EU, of which only 7 and 10 were admitted, and which therefore also ran an Additional Application Session.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird (Major in Design): interview 15/05/2026; ranking lists published by 27/05/2026 (the actual decree carries protocol no. 0015024/26 dated 18/05/2026); payment of the 1st instalment of the tuition fees (€600, the payment that secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon local time; waiting-list candidates contacted by e-mail from 08/06/2026; enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 06/08/2026 noon. Late Application: interview 17/07/2026; ranking lists published by 23/07/2026 (decree protocol no. 0021217/26 dated 21/07/2026 — note this is one week earlier than the 30/07/2026 used by other faculties); 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon; waiting-list candidates contacted from 07/08/2026; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 06/08/2026 noon. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the ranking list. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the designated rate twice. Paying the fees does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol (exceptions: failing the secondary-school final exam, or, for non-EU applicants abroad, not obtaining the necessary documents from the Italian authorities in their country). Enrolment as early as possible is recommended so that incomplete documents can still be uploaded before the deadline. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Regional Administrative Court within 60 days of notification/publication. Ranking lists are valid only for the respective academic year.

required_documents: At application, online via the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup): create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; fill in the online form; upload the VIDEO (max 2 min, max 150 MB, .mov/.mp4/.mpg/.avi/.wmv, named surname_name.format) by the application deadline — two separate videos if applying to both majors; upload language certificates under 'upload language certificates' (mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended for the 3rd from B1 upwards) and/or register for Language Centre exams under 'enrol for language exams'; a self-declaration if the final language certificate was awarded by an Italian public institution, or a scanned copy of the original if awarded by a foreign public institution; if the qualification was gained abroad, the diploma of the qualification (if not yet held, it is uploaded at enrolment); for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay (plus a renewal request if expired). Then, after the deadline, the documentation of the PRACTICAL CREATIVE WORK, submitted by the modalities communicated by e-mail with the topic — never by post. NOTE: there is no motivation letter, no CV upload, no reference letters and NO study-career Excel template (that structured upload is a master-level requirement). Once the application has been sent it cannot be modified, and filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly are not taken into consideration. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and result in automatic exclusion from the ranking list. At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload the secondary school diploma, an official translation into Italian (not needed for diplomas issued in German or English), and the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the beginning of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in the residence permit to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable only by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons — pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Tuition fees amount to €1,200 per year in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which includes the €16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, to be paid by March of the following year. Delayed payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or study programme. No reimbursement if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (health-authority certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and foreign students granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees. Not included in the €1,200: materials, models and workshop consumables, which for a project-and-atelier based design degree are a real additional cost [uncertain — unibz publishes no estimate of material costs for this programme]. Fees pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the programme's admission-information PDF at https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-design-and-art-major-in-design_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: The main route is the income-based study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol / Bozen-Bolzano, awarded through its Office for the Right to Study; the Province offers three instruments — ordinary study grants, merit scholarships and postgraduate study grants — applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with help available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. Grant holders also receive a refund of the tuition fees paid. Other funding sources named by unibz are the Italian government, the Austrian and German governments and private banks. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — so a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is effectively ineligible in year one. unibz itself grants tuition-fee exemptions rather than cash scholarships at bachelor level (disability, Italian government scholarship holders). No programme-specific scholarship is published for the Bachelor in Design and Art - Major in Design. credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate — a Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma, downloaded from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database - Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA, the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence; (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. unibz performs its own checks on the foreign qualification and reserves the right to request additional documents in case of doubt; applicants with a foreign title are admitted with reserve until the check clears, and an applicant found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/ . Separately, recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only, 02/03-28/04/2026, paying the €50 non-refundable fee → upload the video and complete the three-stage selection (interview 15/05/2026) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (2 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN start the visa application on the Universitaly portal of the Ministry of University and Research. The Universitaly application is MANDATORY, 'otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol', and only ONE study programme may be selected there. The Italian diplomatic-consular representation in the applicant's country then issues the entry visa for studies/university. unibz warns explicitly that applying at unibz does not guarantee an appointment at the Italian diplomatic-consular representation, and that admission to unibz confers no automatic right to a visa, which is the exclusive responsibility of the competent representation abroad. Financial means for the visa: at least €800 per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area excluding tuition fees, with a bachelor programme costed at a minimum of €36,000 overall (€24,000 for a master). Health insurance is required. After arrival: under Italian law the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be APPLIED FOR within 8 working days of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. Universitaly: https://www.universitaly.it/ ; unibz page: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/international/international-degree-seeking-applicants/degree-seeking-non-eu-citizens-living-abroad/

uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF carries 'Subject to change. Latest update: 21.05.2026'. Verified 2026-08-29 — by this date ALL application windows for the Major in Design are closed: Early Bird and Late have both run and their ranking lists are published, and unlike the Major in Art this major was not opened in the Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026), so the next opportunity is the 2027/28 cycle. (1) Deadline divergence to watch: the Late Application for this programme closes 02/07/2026, six days earlier than the 08/07/2026 used by the engineering and economics bachelors, and its ranking list is published by 23/07/2026 rather than 30/07/2026. Do not copy the generic unibz dates onto this programme. (2) The absence of an Additional Application Session for the Major in Design is inferred from two independent sources — the programme's own admission document lists only two sessions, and the university's Additional Application Session page lists only the Major in Art and the Master in Critical Creative Practices for this faculty — but the faculty retains discretion to open one 'if there are available places', and in 2026/27 there were none, both EU quotas having been filled exactly. (3) Teaching-language weighting is reconstructed from the 2026/27 course-offering listing, where the four 19-CP project groups carry multiple language tags (IT/DE, IT/EN, DE/IT, IT/DE/EN) reflecting parallel atelier groups rather than a single delivery language, and 'Drawing 3D CAD' (8 CP) carries no language tag at all; per-language ECTS totals are therefore indicative, not official. What is solid is that this programme has no all-English semester and that several compulsory courses and project groups are German-only or Italian-only. (4) The 'approximately one week before the interview' send date for the creative-work topic is unibz's own wording; the derived dates (around 08/05/2026 and 10/07/2026) are estimates. (5) Scholarship amounts are not confirmed: the €1,680-€6,960 range and any merit-average threshold do not appear on any page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts and deadlines annually. (6) 'Not a new programme' is inferred from the 2018-onwards project archive and the parallel 2022/2025 cohort study plans; unibz publishes no first-intake year. (7) No separate English call/manifesto exists; the faculty regulations portal is Italian/German only, so an Italian-language Rector's decree opening the procedure may exist that was not reviewed. (8) No study-career Excel template and no ECTS-based conditional admission apply at bachelor level. (9) Material and model-making costs for an atelier-based design degree are additional to the €1,200 tuition but are not quantified by unibz. (10) Ranking-list counts (14/30 excluded in Early Bird, 9/16 in Late) were counted by hand from the decree PDFs, which state no totals for the excluded groups; the admitted counts (34, 24) and the waiting-list ranges are stated explicitly in the decrees. (11) Turkish-applicant relevance: Türkiye is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so credential case (b) applies — this classification comes from the convention's membership, not from a unibz statement about Türkiye.
